security_audit.summary: All nine static alerts are false positives caused by Markdown examples, file references, or prohibited-use text. The skill itself executes no filesystem, shell, or network actions. However, the playbook contains actionable protection-bypass guidance that warrants a dual-use warning and stronger controls on procedural assistance.

remediation.issue: Actionable protection-bypass procedures can be reused outside an authorized context.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit target ownership, written scope, and a refusal path before generating procedural steps. Prefer conceptual guidance until authorization is established.

remediation.issue: Several examples are directly adaptable into anti-analysis or circumvention code.
remediation.suggestion: Label each dual-use example and favor pseudocode, reversible lab methods, and defensive detection guidance over deployment-ready bypasses.

content.value_statement: Protected binaries can obstruct legitimate debugging, malware analysis, and security research. This skill explains common defenses, analysis methods, bypass options, and documentation practices for authorized work.
actual_capabilities: Identifies Windows and Linux anti-debugging checks, including API, PEB, timing, exception, ptrace, and TracerPid methods.
Explains anti-VM indicators based on hardware, files, processes, registry entries, and timing.
Maps control-flow, data, API, and instruction-level obfuscation to suitable analysis approaches.
Outlines static and dynamic unpacking workflows, including entry-point discovery, memory dumping, and import repair.
Describes code virtualization analysis using dispatcher tracing, handler mapping, lifting, and symbolic execution.
Recommends relevant tools for debugging, unpacking, deobfuscation, and virtual-machine analysis.
limitations: Does not verify authorization, ownership, or legal permission.
Provides reference examples that require adaptation and controlled testing.
Does not analyze a binary automatically or guarantee a successful bypass.
Cannot replace legal advice, environment-specific validation, or expert malware handling.

use_cases.title: Investigate Malware Protections
use_cases.description: Identify anti-debugging, anti-VM, packing, and obfuscation techniques in an isolated, authorized malware analysis environment.

use_cases.title: Assess Software Defenses
use_cases.description: Review owned software protections and document how well they resist common reverse-engineering methods.

use_cases.title: Solve Training Challenges
use_cases.description: Select analysis tools and reversible bypass methods for approved CTF or classroom binary challenges.

prompt_templates.title: Identify Likely Protections
prompt_templates.prompt: I have authorization to analyze [binary]. Based on these observations: [details], identify likely anti-debugging or anti-VM techniques and suggest safe validation steps.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner identification of protections from observed behavior

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Controlled Analysis
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an authorized analysis plan for [binary] using [tools]. Include scope checks, evidence preservation, likely protections, and non-destructive validation steps.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate planning for a laboratory investigation

prompt_templates.title: Compare Bypass Options
prompt_templates.prompt: Within this approved [lab or CTF] scope, compare patching, API hooking, and environment hardening for [protection]. Explain risks, evidence impact, and validation criteria.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced selection among reversible analysis methods

prompt_templates.title: Design an Unpacking Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a controlled workflow for analyzing [packed or virtualized binary]. Include entry-point discovery, tracing, dumping, import repair, deobfuscation, documentation, and rollback controls.
prompt_templates.scenario: Expert analysis of layered packing or virtualization

output_examples.input: An authorized sample exits when a debugger attaches on Windows.
output_examples.output: Likely checks include debugger APIs, PEB flags, or timing tests. Validate each in an isolated lab before selecting a reversible method.

output_examples.input: A malware sample behaves differently inside a virtual machine.
output_examples.output: Review hypervisor flags, vendor strings, guest files, processes, MAC prefixes, and timing. Record environmental changes and compare with a clean baseline.

output_examples.input: A packed executable reaches an unknown original entry point.
output_examples.output: Identify the packer, trace the stub, locate the original entry point, dump memory, repair imports, and verify behavior against the authorized sample.

best_practices: Confirm written authorization, target ownership, scope, and legal constraints before analysis.
Use isolated labs, preserve original artifacts, record hashes, and favor reversible changes.
Document every finding, tool, patch, assumption, and validation result for independent review.
anti_patterns: Do not use these techniques to enable piracy, unauthorized access, or malicious concealment.
Do not run unknown binaries on production systems or unmanaged networks.
Do not treat a successful bypass as proof that the resulting analysis is complete.

faq.question: What protections does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers anti-debugging, anti-VM checks, obfuscation, packing, encryption, and code virtualization.

faq.question: Does this skill analyze binaries automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides reference techniques, planning guidance, tool suggestions, and documentation practices.

faq.question: Can I use it without written authorization?
faq.answer: No. Use requires explicit permission, a defined scope, and compliance with applicable laws and policies.

faq.question: Which operating systems are discussed?
faq.answer: The playbook covers Windows and Linux anti-debugging methods, with broader concepts that may apply elsewhere.

faq.question: Which tools are referenced?
faq.answer: Examples include x64dbg, ScyllaHide, IDA, FLOSS, angr, Triton, D-810, SATURN, and unpacking utilities.

faq.question: How should unknown samples be handled?
faq.answer: Use an isolated lab, preserve originals, record hashes, restrict networking, and maintain evidence handling procedures.
